minutes.headline: Commission authorized Hickory Hills Lake to treat blue-green algae with copper and approved Lake Shirley's plan.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission heard a Select Board member's objection to funding a survey of an alleged encroachment and agreed the chair would review aerial photos for other encroachments. It authorized copper sulfate treatment at Hickory Hills Lake and approved the Lake Shirley treatment plan. It held several wetland hearings, approved two notices of intent and a Howard Street driveway, and continued the rest.

what_happened.line: The Commission voted by roll call, all aye, to authorize Hickory Hills Lake to work with the agent on a copper sulfate treatment for blue-green algae.
It approved the Lake Shirley annual treatment plan by roll call, all aye.
After a Select Board member objected to paying for an encroachment survey, members agreed without objection that the chair will review aerial photos of conservation land.
It approved the Pine Grove Road notice of intent and the Howard Street driveway. A vote on Highland Street was later rescinded because two members were ineligible to vote.
Hearings for 398 Sunset Lane, 101 Pleasant Street, 52 Street, 48 Pearl Street and 137 Flynn Road were continued, most to August 4 or 18.

why_it_matters: Algae treatment and its testing draw on limited funds, and the Commission said testing would be capped, so lake users may see less monitoring.
Land bought with state self-help money could oblige the town to repay the state if use conditions are violated, which would fall on the town budget, mostly taxes.
The 326 Highland Street approval was rescinded after the vote, so that application has no valid approval from this meeting in the minutes.
watch_next: The August 4 and August 18 hearings, including 101 Pleasant Street, 398 Sunset Lane, 48 Pearl Street and 137 Flynn Road.
The chair's aerial photo review of conservation properties and the Table Rock land use plan hearing, both due at the next meeting.
